scope: Proposition A.5 (Finite-horizon reconstruction) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Starting with X, perform finitely many compatible regular splits as in Theorem A.1. For the first split require locally finite compact radial wall and side components. At the later split for color i, require the defining functions to be positive on the inverse image of Ai and negative on the inverse image of Bi, with those inverse images contained in open regions of the stipulated signs. After any r ≥ 1 of these splits, the diagram has a reconstruction Xr, obtained by finite collar truncations and gluing at hit faces, with the following properties: (i) Xr is a smooth manifold homeomorphic to X. Its r labelled walls are closed smooth hypersur- faces with simultaneous transverse intersection charts. Each wall component is compact, the component families are locally finite, and the closed sign/hit pieces are exactly the compact cornered truncations of the analytic packets, by components. (ii) The packet maps glue to a proper continuous map qr : Xr → X. There is a homeomorphism Hr : Xr → X such that d0 Hr(z), qr(z)  ≤ r (z ∈ Xr). (A.4) (iii) Horizons can be enlarged to exceed any already specified compatible product thresholds on the full analytic packets. A horizon is constant for all occurrences of a normal coordinate belonging to one connected global wall component. Such enlargement has an identification with the previous reconstruction which preserves qr, every old wall, and every old side status. (iv) Once color i has been processed, q−1 r (Ai) remains in its open positive phase and q−1 r (Bi) remains in its open negative phase at every subsequent stage. In particular its wall misses q−1 r (Ai ∪ Bi).
